unsupported_claims: Gains flatten out somewhere around 100 to 200 dimensions for most tasks (general literature claim not in the evidence; the paper says around 100).
Continued gains are more plausible with large graphs, many-class tasks, and rich training data such as longer walks.
Longer walks supply more co-occurrence context so higher dimensions can keep helping; with short walks extra dimensions add little or overfit, so the benefit depends on walk length.
rationale: The answer never corrects the false premise that performance keeps rising past about 100 dimensions; the paper says it saturates around 100. It instead speculates about conditions and walk-length interactions the evidence does not support, and treats the premise as plausible.
